message:
Please review the following document.

Here is how its author describes it:

<author>
This bid is unusual in that it is not based on assumptions about demand: we tested the exact opening pattern at Ashgrove before asking for a penny, and measured the results hour by hour. The pilot showed strong uptake, with evening visits running close to daytime levels and Sunday sessions very popular with families, and new memberships up by about two-thirds on the year before. That gives Members real local evidence that the hours will be used. The costing is equally careful. Staffing is built up from first principles, hours times staff times weeks times branches at the correct graded rate with on-costs, and utilities are taken from actual pilot spend rather than estimates, all of which sums to £174,000. We also looked seriously at the cheaper self-service alternative and explain why it would cost more once building works are included. I am confident this is a well-tested, carefully costed proposal that delivers on the Council Plan.
</author>

<document>
Budget Justification: Extended Opening Hours at Five Branch Libraries, 2027-28
Library Services, Westmoor Borough Council, September 2026

1. Request
Library Services requests a growth bid of £174,000 in the 2027-28 revenue budget to extend opening hours at five branch libraries (Ashgrove, Fenwick, Holt Lane, Kingsmead and Millbrook) by ten hours a week each, from 38 to 48 hours.

2. Rationale
The five branches currently close at 5 pm on weekdays and do not open on Sundays. Residents' surveys have repeatedly identified opening hours as the main barrier to library use among working-age adults: in the 2025 Residents' Survey, 44% of non-users aged 25-54 said the library "is never open when I can go". The Council Plan commits to increasing library use among working-age residents and to supporting adult learning and job-seeking.

Each branch would add late opening until 8 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays (six additional hours) and Sunday opening from 11 am to 3 pm (four additional hours).

3. Evidence from the Ashgrove pilot
From October 2025 to March 2026, Ashgrove trialled exactly this pattern, funded from one-off underspends.

Table 1. Ashgrove pilot: average visits per opening hour, October 2025 to March 2026
Time slot | Visits per hour
Weekday 9 am - 12 pm | 46
Weekday 12 pm - 5 pm | 58
Tuesday and Thursday 5 pm - 8 pm (new) | 21
Saturday 9 am - 1 pm | 64
Sunday 11 am - 3 pm (new) | 52

Over the pilot, Ashgrove recorded 1,140 new library memberships, compared with 690 in the same months a year earlier. Sunday sessions were particularly popular with families, and a weekly job club in the Thursday evening slot was fully booked from its third week.

Evening visits at Ashgrove averaged close to the weekday daytime level, which shows that there is strong latent demand for evening opening and that the new hours will be well used across all five branches.

4. Costs
Additional hours need two staff on duty at all times, in line with the Council's lone-working policy. Staffing is calculated on 50 weeks a year, allowing for bank holiday closures.

Table 2. Cost of extended hours, five branches
Item | Basis | Cost
Staffing | 10 hours x 2 staff x 50 weeks x 5 branches = 5,000 hours at £24.80 per hour (including on-costs) | £124,000
Utilities and caretaking | £6,500 per branch | £32,500
Self-service kiosk upgrades (maintenance contract) | 5 branches | £7,500
Total | | £174,000

The staffing rate is the mid-point of the Library Assistant grade plus 28% on-costs and an enhancement for Sunday working. Utilities and caretaking costs are based on the actual additional costs recorded at Ashgrove during the pilot, scaled to a full year.

5. Value for money
At current visit rates, the extra hours across the five branches would generate roughly 84,000 additional visits a year, at a cost of around £2 per visit. This compares favourably with the borough's average cost per library visit of £3.40.

6. Alternatives considered
We considered opening the branches with self-service access only in the extra hours, as some authorities have done. This would cut staffing costs by around two-thirds, but the Council's insurers have advised that unstaffed opening would require building alterations and CCTV at an estimated £60,000 per branch, and it would not support the job club and family activities that drove much of the pilot's success.

7. Risks
Recruitment. We expect to fill most additional hours from existing part-time staff who have asked for more hours, as happened during the pilot.
Demand at other branches. Ashgrove is our busiest branch, and demand at the other four may be lower. We will review usage after six months.

8. Conclusion
The twelve-month Ashgrove pilot has demonstrated strong demand for evening and Sunday opening, with new memberships up by two-thirds and evening use close to daytime levels. We ask Members to approve a growth bid of £174,000 to extend this successful model to all five branches from April 2027.
</document>
response:
## Summary of the bid

Library Services asks for £174,000 a year from 2027-28 to add ten hours a week at five branch libraries: Tuesday and Thursday evenings until 8 pm, and Sundays from 11 am to 3 pm. The case rests on three things:
- residents' survey evidence that current hours deter working-age adults;
- a pilot of exactly this pattern at Ashgrove;
- a cost per extra visit of about £2, against a borough average of £3.40.

## Verdict

The case for Sunday opening is well supported. The case for evening opening is not. The pilot data show evenings are the weakest slot by a wide margin, yet the text and the author's summary describe the opposite. The cost table also doesn't add to the total requested. Both need correcting before the bid goes to Members.

## 1. The cost table doesn't sum to £174,000

£124,000 + £32,500 + £7,500 = **£164,000**, not £174,000. The individual lines check out: 5,000 hours × £24.80 = £124,000, and £6,500 × 5 = £32,500. Either a cost line is missing or the total is wrong by £10,000. It needs resolving either way, since Members will be approving the total.

## 2. The pilot shows weak evening demand, not strong demand

Table 1 shows 21 visits an hour on weekday evenings, against 46 to 58 during weekday daytimes. That is **less than half the quietest daytime slot**. Yet three passages describe evening use as close to daytime:
- Section 3: "Evening visits at Ashgrove averaged close to the weekday daytime level"
- Section 8: "evening use close to daytime levels"
- the author's summary: "evening visits running close to daytime levels"

It is **Sundays** that run close to daytime levels, at 52 an hour. The text seems to have transferred the Sunday result to evenings.

The difference matters for value for money. Splitting the costs by slot, using the bid's own figures:

| | Staff hours a year (5 branches) | Staffing cost | Visits a year (at Ashgrove rates) | Staffing cost per visit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Evenings (6 h/wk) | 3,000 | £74,400 | 31,500 | ≈ £2.36 |
| Sundays (4 h/wk) | 2,000 | £49,600 | 52,000 | ≈ £0.95 |

Each evening visit costs about two and a half times as much in staffing as a Sunday visit, and that is before utilities. On the bid's own evidence, the strongest case is for Sunday opening at all five branches. Evenings could be added more selectively, for example on Thursdays only, where the job club was fully booked.

## 3. Ashgrove's results are applied to all five branches

The value-for-money figure is correct as arithmetic: 334 visits a week × 50 weeks × 5 branches ≈ 84,000 visits. But it assumes every branch matches Ashgrove, which the risks section describes as "our busiest branch". Section 3's claim that the hours "will be well used across all five branches" contradicts that caveat.

Two further reasons the 84,000 figure is probably too high:
- **Not all visits are new.** Some people visiting in the new hours would otherwise have come at another time. The net gain in visits is lower than the gross count.
- **Average and marginal costs aren't comparable.** The £3.40 borough average includes buildings, stock and management. The £2 figure covers only the extra costs of opening longer. The comparison flatters the bid.

## 4. The pilot's length and the membership figure

- **The pilot ran six months, not twelve.** It ran October 2025 to March 2026, but the conclusion calls it a "twelve-month Ashgrove pilot".
- **The membership rise has no comparison.** New memberships rose from 690 to 1,140, an increase of 65%, so "about two-thirds" is right. But nothing shows how much of this came from the extra hours. The bid should show what happened to membership at the other four branches over the same months. If they rose too, something borough-wide is at least part of the explanation.

## 5. The self-service alternative is not shown to cost more

The author's summary says the bid explains why self-service "would cost more once building works are included". The document doesn't show this, and its own figures suggest otherwise:
- **Annual saving.** Cutting staffing by two-thirds saves about £83,000 a year.
- **One-off cost.** Building works are about £60,000 × 5 = £300,000, and that is capital rather than revenue spending.
- **Break-even.** Self-service becomes cheaper after about three and a half years.

That may still be the wrong choice. Self-service wouldn't support the job club or family activities, and capital may be harder to find. But that is a judgement Members should make with the figures in front of them.

The low evening use also points to a mixed option: staffed Sundays, self-service on most evenings, and staffed evenings only where a programmed activity like the job club needs them.

## 6. Smaller points to clarify

- **Current hours.** Table 1 implies weekday opening 9 am to 5 pm (40 hours) plus Saturday 9 am to 1 pm (4 hours), which is 44 hours, not 38. Perhaps one branch closes on a weekday or half-day. Worth checking, since "38 to 48" appears in the request itself.
- **Kiosk maintenance.** The cost table includes £7,500 for kiosk upgrades, but the bid rejects self-service opening. It should say why the extra hours need it.
- **Staff rate.** A single rate including a Sunday enhancement is applied to all 5,000 hours. If the enhancement is averaged in, fine. If it applies to every hour, evenings are overcosted.
- **Missing staff costs.** The table has no allowance for annual leave on the extra contracted hours, time to open and close the building, or supervision. Some may sit within the 28% on-costs. It should say.
- **Utilities are probably overstated.** The figure scales winter costs (October to March) up to a full year, which likely overstates heating and lighting. That errs in the bid's favour as a prudent assumption, and could be noted as such.

## 7. What is sound

- **Strong evidence of need.** The survey finding that 44% of non-users aged 25–54 say "never open when I can go" is directly relevant and ties clearly to the Council Plan.
- **A real pilot.** Testing the exact pattern before asking for money is good practice and gives real local data.
- **Strong Sunday results.** At 52 visits an hour, Sundays are close to daytime use, cheap per visit, and backed by the families finding.
- **The job club.** Being fully booked from week three is real evidence of evening demand for programmed activity, even if casual evening use is low.
- **Sound staffing basis.** Hours × staff × weeks × branches is correctly worked. The lone-working requirement is a legitimate reason for two staff.

## 8. The author's description vs. the document

- **"Evening visits running close to daytime levels."** Evening visits are 21 an hour against 46–58 in the daytime.
- **"Sums to £174,000."** The lines sum to £164,000.
- **"Explain why [self-service] would cost more."** The bid's own figures show it costs less after about three and a half years.

## Recommendations

1. Fix the total, or add the missing £10,000 line.
2. Correct the description of evening use in Sections 3 and 8, and report evenings and Sundays separately in the value-for-money section.
3. Present membership and visit trends at the other four branches, and scale the visit estimate down to reflect them.
4. Correct "twelve-month" to six months.
5. Set out the self-service comparison in figures over several years, including a mixed option.
6. Consider restructuring the bid with Sundays at all five branches and evenings tied to programmed activity. On this evidence, that is the strongest version of the proposal and probably cheaper.

I can redraft the value-for-money section with the evening and Sunday split, or set out the options comparison as a table for Members.
